title: The $\varepsilon$-smoothed Entanglement of Formation and its relation to the Moreau-Yosida approximation
abstract: We describe a family of convex continuous functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, on the set of states of a bipartite quantum system (consisting of finite-dimensional or infinite-dimensional subsystems) obtained by applying the Mora-Piani-Briegel construction of $\varepsilon$-measure (proposed in [Phys. Rev. A 109, 052413]) to the Entanglement of Formation (EoF) with the use of the trace norm distance in the role of basic metric. These functions are non-increasing in $\varepsilon$ and converge pointwise to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$. We conducted a detailed analysis of properties of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, using (among others) the relationship between the family $\{E_{F,\varepsilon}\}_{\varepsilon\in[0,1]}$ and the family $\{E^λ_F(ρ)\}_{λ>0}$ of Moreau-Yosida approximations of the EoF explored in [arXiv:2609.30246].   We obtain a variational expression for the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ (which for $\varepsilon=0$ turns into the standard variational expression for the EoF). We also describe the weak subadditivity property of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ and analyse their continuity properties.   The semicontinuity bounds for the EoF (presented in [Lob.J.Math., 46, 2632-2658],[arXiv:2404.07978]) allow us to obtain easily computable upper bounds on the rate of uniform convergence of the function $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$ on the sets of states with bounded rank/energy of one of the marginal states.   Applicability of the obtained results to other entanglement measures, in particular, to the relative entropy of entanglement, is discussed.   As an auxiliary result, it is shown that for any state of an infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system, there exists a nearest separable state w.r.t. the trace norm distance. The non-uniqueness of such a state is also shown.
summary: This paper develops a mathematical framework to study the Entanglement of Formation ($	ext{EoF}$) by introducing an $\varepsilon$-smoothed version, $	ext{EF}_{\varepsilon}$. It rigorously connects this smoothed measure to the Moreau-Yosida approximation, proving convergence properties and establishing variational formulas. This work provides powerful tools for analyzing entanglement in both finite and infinite-dimensional quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the $\varepsilon$-smoothed version of the Entanglement of Formation ($	ext{EoF}$) and establishes its rigorous mathematical relationship to the Moreau-Yosida approximation of the $	ext{EoF}$.
main_result: It proves that the $\varepsilon$-smoothed function $	ext{EF}_{\varepsilon}(ho)$ is non-increasing in $\varepsilon$ and converges pointwise to the true $	ext{EoF}$ as $\varepsilon 	o 0^+$, while also deriving a variational expression for it.
method: The analysis employs convex analysis, relating the $\varepsilon$-smoothing via the Mora-Piani-Briegel construction to the Moreau-Yosida approximation using the trace norm distance as the metric.
model_or_system: The study concerns bipartite quantum systems (AB) described by density matrices $ho$, applicable to both finite and infinite-dimensional subsystems.
key_observables: Entanglement of Formation ($	ext{EoF}$), $\varepsilon$-smoothed $	ext{EoF}$ ($	ext{EF}_{\varepsilon}$), and the trace-norm distance to separable states ($d(ho, \mathcal{S}_{	ext{AB}}^{	ext{sep}})$).
important_parameters: The smoothing parameter $\varepsilon \in (0, 1]$ and the approximation parameter $\lambda > 0$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the properties of convex, lower semi-continuous functions and the existence of nearest separable states in the trace norm for infinite dimensions.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the $\varepsilon$-smoothed $	ext{EoF}$ and relates it to the Moreau-Yosida approximation. It then derives variational expressions and proves properties like weak subadditivity and convergence rates as $\varepsilon 	o 0^+$. Finally, it discusses applicability to other entanglement measures.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical treatment of entanglement measures using regularization and approximation techniques is fundamental for quantifying quantum correlations in complex systems, bridging abstract functional analysis with physical observables.
